job.domain: Singapore F&B discovery — Telegram bot replies, inline-keyboard buttons, and Mini-App UI chrome
job._comment: One file per target language. google_translation MUST be filled by a real Cloud Translation v3 call before Gemini sees the file — if the same model both translates and audits, the audit only catches errors it does not itself share.

glossary._comment: do_not_translate is a hard mechanical rule. preferred is grounded in strings already shipped in web/cuisine/src/v2/lib/i18n.js — the Mini App and the bot must not diverge.

preferred._comment: Target-language column. Swap this whole object per language file.

items.context: Status on a venue card, meaning the eatery is currently within its trading hours. Not 'open' in the sense of unlocked or available.

gemini_audit.notes: Matches the shipped Mini-App wording exactly, so bot and TMA agree.

items.source: 🚆 For trains, buses, and getting around Singapore, tap /transport. This chat searches for food and eateries.
items.context: Sent when someone types a transport question into the food-search chat. /transport is a literal Telegram command the user must tap or type.
items.google_translation: 🚆 有关火车、巴士和在新加坡出行的信息，请点按 /运输。此聊天搜索食物和餐馆。

gemini_audit.corrected: 🚆 查询地铁、巴士和新加坡出行，请点按 /transport。此聊天用于搜索美食和餐馆。
gemini_audit.back_translation: 🚆 For information about trains, buses and getting around Singapore, please tap /transport [rendered as the Chinese word for 'transport']. This chat searches for food and restaurants.

issues.detail: /transport became /运输. Telegram will not recognise it, so the one action the message exists to offer is dead. The command is literal input, not a word.
'trains' rendered as 火车 (inter-city rail). In Singapore the user means the MRT — 地铁.

gemini_audit.notes: The back_translation is what exposes the command break — the Chinese reads perfectly well right up to the point where nothing happens when you tap it.

items.context: Crowd indicator on a venue card: many diners there right now. Not 'busy' as in occupied, unavailable, or hard at work.

gemini_audit.back_translation: 🔴 busy / occupied (a person with much to do)

issues.detail: 忙碌 describes a person having a lot to do. The card means the place is crowded with diners.
The Mini App already renders this concept as 拥挤. Two surfaces would label the same signal differently in one session.

gemini_audit.notes: Adopting the shipped wording resolves both issues at once.

items.source: ⏳ You've hit the limit of {cap} requests per 15 minutes. Try again in ~{mins} min.
items.context: Refusal sent when a user exceeds the per-chat rate limit. {cap} is the ceiling, {mins} the whole minutes until the fixed window rolls over.
items.google_translation: ⏳ 您已达到每 15 分钟 {上限} 次请求的限制。请在约 {分钟} 分钟后重试。

gemini_audit.corrected: ⏳ 您已达到每 15 分钟 {cap} 次请求的上限。请在约 {mins} 分钟后重试。
gemini_audit.back_translation: ⏳ You have reached the limit of {上限} requests per 15 minutes. Please retry in about {分钟} minutes.

issues.detail: {cap} → {上限} and {mins} → {分钟}. The substitution keys no longer match, so the user is shown the literal braces instead of the numbers — the only two facts the message carries.

gemini_audit.notes: Prose is fine; the message is still broken. Placeholder damage is invisible in review unless you check the braces character by character.

items.source: ✨ Top {n} eateries near {place} (within {km} km, ranked by rating · Michelin · rarity · crowd)
items.context: Header above a fan-out list of nearby eateries. Sent with parse_mode HTML.

gemini_audit.notes: Seed state, shipped in the template on purpose. An item that has not been through Cloud Translation must stay visibly unjudged rather than default to pass.

summary._comment: Filled by the auditor at the end. Counts must add up to items.length — a total that does not reconcile means something was skipped silently.
